issues.description: HAS_NUMERIC regex misses numeric weights outside the named-keyword map (e.g. 250, 550).
issues.detail: HAS_NUMERIC is built only from NUMERIC_TO_NAMED.keys() which is 100..900 in steps of 100. A declaration like `font-weight: 550` (valid CSS, valid input for named-where-possible) will fail the pre-test and bail out, silently skipping a value the rule used to warn on. The fast-path changes observable behavior. Use \d to match any numeric token, or just /\d/.

issues.description: import-notation `url` short-circuit drops the invalid-string warning path.
issues.detail: The old rule walked into valueParser and could report on string-form imports even when primary is 'url'. New `if (primary === 'url' && /url\(/i.test(params)) return;` exits before any check, meaning a malformed url() (e.g. with stray nodes) is no longer parsed. Confirm there is no diagnostic the early return now suppresses; otherwise the perf win comes at correctness cost.

issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex is unanchored and case-sensitive in a way inconsistent with HAS_KEYWORD.
issues.detail: HAS_PERCENTAGE uses `(?:^|[,\s])` and no `i` flag; HAS_KEYWORD uses `\b` and `i`. Keyframe selectors are ASCII so it works, but the asymmetry will bite a maintainer six months from now wondering why one is anchored and the other isn't. Pick one shape and document why.

issues.description: walkRules(/:/) over-matches; nearly every selector contains a colon somewhere harmless.
issues.detail: Combinators, attribute selectors with pseudo-class-looking values, and any rule with a `:hover` will pass the filter. The filter is essentially a no-op on real stylesheets, so the perf gain is small while the regex adds indirection. Either keep the original `includes(':')` check (it was fine) or tighten to `/::?[a-z]/i`.

The pattern matches any `min-` or `max-` substring, including things like `max-width` inside calc expressions or future feature names that aren't range-notation. Acceptable as a pre-filter because the real parse runs after, but worth a comment explaining it is a coarse filter, not a correctness check.

issues.description: Module-scope RegExp construction relies on import order of keyword arrays.
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED is built at module load from imported sets. If anyone later lazy-loads those references or reorders exports, the regex silently becomes wrong with no test failure at the rule boundary. A short comment, or building the regex inside the rule closure on first call, would make the dependency explicit.

review.summary: The patch is the right shape: cheap pre-filters before expensive value/selector parsing. Most of it is good taste — `walkRules(/:not\(/i, ...)` is exactly the kind of small change a maintainer wants. But two of the fast paths change observable behavior: HAS_NUMERIC only knows 100..900 so non-canonical weights slip through, and the import-notation `url` branch returns before the parser can flag malformed url(). Fix those and tighten the asymmetric regex shapes; the rest is fine. NEEDS-WORK, not REFUSE.
